findings.title: Copy-paste bug: rawTokenId null-check is never performed
isAccessTokenId() grant-shortcut check is logically inverted and off-by-one, so it never actually validates the grant type
findings.body:
The new helper `isAccessTokenId(String expectedGrantShortcut)` is supposed to verify that the encoded access-token id contains the expected grant-type shortcut (at positions 4-5 of the 6-character context prefix, per DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider's encoding: sessionType[0-1] + tokenType[2-3] + grantType[4-5]). The implementation has two combined defects:
1. It extracts `items[0].substring(3, 5)` instead of `substring(4, 6)`, so it reads the wrong characters (half of the tokenType shortcut and half of the grantType shortcut) rather than the actual grant-type shortcut.
2. The condition is inverted: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns a non-match precisely when the (wrongly extracted) substring equals the expected value, instead of returning a non-match when it does NOT equal the expected value.
Because of the wrong substring range, the extracted characters will essentially never equal `expectedGrantShortcut`, so the `if` branch is effectively never taken and the method degenerates into validating only that the raw id part is a UUID. This means all the call sites that were updated to use this helper (expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectAuthReqIdToToken) do not actually assert that the correct grant-type shortcut was embedded in the token id, silently defeating the purpose of the new assertion and hiding future regressions in the grant-type encoding.

findings.title: New mandatory getShortcut() method breaks existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations
findings.body: A new abstract method `String getShortcut();` was added to the OAuth2GrantTypeFactory provider-factory interface with no default implementation. Any existing third-party/custom implementation of this SPI (grant types are a documented extension point) will fail to compile/deploy until it implements this new method, and any already-compiled custom provider will throw AbstractMethodError at runtime when loaded against the new interface. This is a breaking SPI change that should at least be called out as such (or given a default implementation) given it is not accompanied by any deprecation path.

findings.title: Backward-incompatible change to access-token id (jti) format is not documented
findings.body: `initToken()` now prefixes every access-token id with a 6-character encoded context (session type + token type + grant type) before the previously plain UUID, e.g. `onrtac:1f65761e-...` instead of a bare UUID. This changes the format of the `jti` claim for every access token issued by Keycloak going forward. Any external system, log parser, SIEM rule, or client integration that validates/parses the token id as a plain UUID (36 chars, specific dash positions) will break. The PR does not include any upgrade-guide note, migration documentation, or changelog entry describing this change in token id format, even though it affects every issued access token by default with no opt-out configuration (only an SPI override is possible, which requires writing custom provider code).

findings.title: Duplicate-shortcut validation logic in postInit() has no test coverage
findings.body: postInit() contains important validation logic that throws an IllegalStateException if two registered OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations collide on id or shortcut (`grantsByShortcuts.size() != grantsToShortcuts.size()`). This is the only safety net preventing silently incorrect token-id decoding when a new grant type is added with a clashing shortcut. The added DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest only exercises DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider with hand-built maps and never calls postInit() with a real (or fake) KeycloakSessionFactory/provider-factory stream, so this validation path is completely untested.
